meta.notes: Core astronomical and calendrical cycles used in astronomy, chronology, and long-term sky modeling.

cycles.name: Metonic Cycle
cycles.description: 19 tropical years are approximately equal to 235 synodic lunar months.
cycles.significance: Foundation for lunisolar calendar reconciliation.

cycles.name: Callippic Cycle
cycles.description: Refinement of four Metonic cycles with leap-day correction.
cycles.significance: Improves long-term lunisolar alignment.

cycles.name: Hipparchic Cycle
cycles.description: Four Callippic cycles used as a higher-order correction block.
cycles.significance: Historical long-cycle refinement in ancient astronomy.

cycles.name: Synodic Month
cycles.description: Average interval between identical lunar phases, such as full moon to full moon.
cycles.significance: Primary month unit in lunar and lunisolar systems.

cycles.name: Draconic Month
cycles.description: Moon's node-to-node period relative to the ecliptic.
cycles.significance: Important for eclipse timing models.

cycles.name: Anomalistic Month
cycles.description: Perigee-to-perigee period of the Moon.
cycles.significance: Affects supermoon timing and lunar distance patterns.

cycles.name: Eclipse Season
cycles.description: Interval between windows when the Sun is near a lunar node.
cycles.significance: Predicts clusters of solar/lunar eclipses.

cycles.name: Saros Cycle
cycles.description: Near-repeat interval for similar eclipses from geometry recurrence.
cycles.significance: Classic eclipse prediction cycle.

cycles.name: Inex Cycle
cycles.description: Longer eclipse recurrence interval connecting different saros families.
cycles.significance: Useful for classifying eclipse series transitions.

cycles.name: Solar Sunspot Cycle
cycles.description: Average magnetic activity cycle of the Sun seen in sunspot counts.
cycles.significance: Drives space weather and auroral activity trends.

cycles.name: Hale Magnetic Cycle
cycles.description: Two sunspot cycles required for solar magnetic polarity to return.
cycles.significance: Long-form solar dynamo period.

cycles.name: Jupiter-Saturn Great Conjunction
cycles.description: Mean interval between conjunctions of Jupiter and Saturn.
cycles.significance: Major marker in historical chronology and sky cycles.

cycles.name: Great Trigon
cycles.description: Successive great conjunctions cycle through similar elemental triplicity patterns over centuries.
cycles.significance: Long-cycle structure derived from Jupiter-Saturn conjunction drift.

cycles.name: Venus Pentagram Cycle
cycles.description: Five synodic Venus cycles align closely with eight Earth years, tracing a pentagram-like pattern.
cycles.significance: Famous resonance in naked-eye planetary astronomy.

cycles.name: Synodic Venus Cycle
cycles.description: Mean interval between consecutive inferior conjunctions of Venus.
cycles.significance: Basis of Venus visibility phases and cycle work.

cycles.name: Halley Comet Cycle
cycles.description: Orbital return interval of 1P/Halley, varying by perturbations.
cycles.significance: Most recognized periodic comet cycle.

cycles.name: Encke Comet Cycle
cycles.description: Orbital return interval of Comet 2P/Encke.
cycles.significance: Classic short-period comet benchmark.

cycles.name: Precession of the Equinoxes
cycles.description: Slow conical motion of Earth's rotation axis relative to fixed stars.
cycles.significance: Shifts equinox positions through zodiacal constellations over millennia.

cycles.name: Great Year (Platonic)
cycles.description: Traditional term for one full precessional cycle of the equinoxes.
cycles.significance: Long-duration epochal framing in astronomy and chronology traditions.

cycles.name: Milankovitch Obliquity Cycle
cycles.description: Variation in Earth's axial tilt angle over tens of millennia.
cycles.significance: Major pacing component in glacial-interglacial climate structure.

cycles.name: Milankovitch Precession Cycle
cycles.description: Seasonal timing shift from axial precession interacting with orbital geometry.
cycles.significance: Controls seasonal insolation pacing over geologic time.

cycles.name: Milankovitch Eccentricity Cycle
cycles.description: Long-term change in orbital ellipse shape from near-circular to more elliptical.
cycles.significance: Dominant long pacing in Quaternary paleoclimate archives.
